take_homes: Access is not use. Licence counts are not adoption, and I should ask what the other person's job actually is.
Before I roll out a tool, ask what would have to be true for this person to drop what they use now.
Check the people side (who owns it, who decides) as hard as the tech. A tidy tech plan next to an empty people plan is a warning.

monday.move: Pick one of my own people who does a job we could hand to an agent, and ask how they do it today. Build nothing yet.
monday.who: One person on my team, probably someone in the sales-support analysis work
monday.when: A short conversation this week, if the calendar allows
monday.stop_condition: If they say what they have works fine and give no reason to change, I drop the idea
monday.blocker: The steering groups for the last programme, and my own doubt that anything sticks

misconception.why: The module does not sell a revolution. It admits that rollouts stall on human reasons and that a real project got no decision. That is not the 2017 slide. I still think much of this will blow over, but 'wait and see' is no longer obviously safe, because I can test the claims on my own team.

one_line: Better than I expected. The failure story and the premortem were honest and practical. The generic AI-landscape paragraphs between them are the same slide we saw for agile.
